phrases: Relay is (to our knowledge) the only benchmark that enforces literal amnesia between turns — each turn is played by a freshly sampled LLM instance with zero continuity except a self-authored baton — rather than treating memory as an add-on module bolted onto a single persistent agent.

Unlike prior compression-bottleneck studies of LLM-to-LLM communication (latent KV-cache relay, Lewis signaling games), Relay is the first to pair a hard, human-legible character/pixel budget with a provably-sound truncated belief-tracker reference, so a budget's survivability is certified analytically rather than just observed empirically.

Relay is the first agent-memory study we're aware of to document constitutional lock-in as a *failure mode*: a model's own self-authored pinned spec measurably underperforms an externally imposed schema, inverting the usual assumption that self-designed conventions beat imposed ones.

Relay's image/pixel-channel condition is the first to dissociate write-render-read fidelity from downstream task performance for LLM-authored visual memory, and to document that models default to writing legible text into images rather than inventing denser spatial encodings.

Where existing memory benchmarks (LoCoMo, MemGym, MemoryArena, MEMTRACK, PrecisionMemBench) score a persistent agent's recall inside its own accumulating context, Relay isolates externalization itself as the only channel across a hard reset — showing it is a capability dissociable from state-tracking competence, not a byproduct of it.

threats.title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents
threats.overlap: Directly compares memory architectures (stateless vs. persistent-notebook) against channel/capacity constraints for LLM agents, using a Lewis signaling game where a sender/receiver must coordinate on a code — conceptually the closest existing paper to Relay's core axis of 'what happens to LLM-to-LLM coordination when you vary what crosses the bottleneck.' It even reports a mechanism resembling notation invention: agents' notebooks 'externalize learned conventions, freeing agents from having to rederive codes each round,' and finds stateless (no persistent notebook) agents collapse at high channel capacity.
threats.differentiation: Their game is cooperative code-coordination (Lewis signaling) between two agents that both want to converge on a shared label, not a hidden-information deduction/state-tracking task with a certified-correct answer; the channel is text-only (no image/pixel condition); there is no budget-matched *sound* reference tracker used to certify which budgets are information-theoretically survivable (they report empirical capacity curves, not a provable-truncation bound); and the paper does not surface self-designed-spec lock-in, per-model crossover from imposed schemas, or write-render-read fidelity dissociation — findings specific to Relay.
threats.claims_to_verify: Confirm from the full paper (not just the abstract) whether their 'stateless' condition literally instantiates a fresh LLM sample every round with no shared context beyond the transmitted message (which would be very close to Relay's baton design) or whether it merely means 'no notebook but same rolling context/continuity within an episode.' Also verify there is no image/SVG channel condition and no formal optimal/sound-reference bound anywhere in the paper before claiming those as clean differentiators.

threats.title: Evolving Interpretable Constitutions for Multi-Agent Coordination
threats.overlap: Reports that one-shot LLM-authored 'constitutions' (self-designed governing rule sets) substantially underperform an alternative (evolutionary-search-refined constitutions) in a multi-agent coordination/survival game — the same qualitative shape as Relay's 'constitutional lock-in' finding that a model's self-designed pinned spec underperforms an imposed schema.
threats.differentiation: The domain is a resource-gathering/survival grid-world with an eliminating 'Overseer,' not a hidden-keyboard deduction or memory-relay task, and the paper's contrast is self-designed-once vs. evolutionarily-optimized-through-iterated-search (an LLM-driven genetic-programming loop), not self-designed vs. experimenter-imposed/harness-validated schema as in Relay. There is no fresh-instance-per-turn relay, no character/pixel transmission budget, and no belief-tracking or notation-drift analysis.
threats.claims_to_verify: Read the full paper to confirm the 'self-designed' baseline is genuinely a single LLM-authored spec (not itself iteratively refined) and that 'evolved' constitutions are produced by a search process rather than an experimenter-fixed schema — if the evolved constitutions are still LLM-authored-and-refined rather than externally imposed, the mechanism behind the underperformance may be closer to Relay's finding than the differentiation above assumes, and the write-up should hedge accordingly.

threats.title: When Less Latent Leads to Better Relay: Information-Preserving Compression for Latent Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
threats.overlap: Uses the word 'Relay' for the exact same conceptual move — compressing what passes between successive LLM agents under a budget — and explicitly frames the problem as bottlenecked hand-off between agents, evaluating multiple compression ratios against task accuracy, which is structurally close to Relay's budget-vs-survivability framing.
threats.differentiation: What crosses the bottleneck is a continuous KV-cache/latent representation (compressed via orthogonal low-rank residual injection), not a human-legible text note or a rendered image — so there is no 'only pixels/characters cross' constraint, no possibility of notation invention or drift (there's no discrete authored artifact to inspect), and no self-authored-spec vs. imposed-schema comparison. Evaluation is on math/QA/coding benchmarks, not a hidden-state deduction game, and there is no sound/provably-optimal reference tracker for certifying budgets.
threats.claims_to_verify: Verify in the full text whether 'fresh' downstream agents are literally freshly sampled model instances (matching Relay's per-turn amnesia) or the same agent continuing with a compressed cache — the abstract doesn't resolve this, and if agents are effectively continuous (just cache-compressed) rather than swapped out, the 'fresh instance' distinction Relay relies on is even more clearly its own contribution.

works.title: MEMTRACK: Evaluating Long-Term Memory and State Tracking in Multi-Platform Dynamic Agent Environments
works.what_it_does: Benchmarks memory/state-tracking for a single persistent agent operating across interleaved enterprise platforms (Slack, Linear, Git), scoring correctness, efficiency, and redundancy; best model (GPT-5) hits only ~60% correctness.
works.delta: Agent keeps its own continuity and full context throughout; Relay instead severs continuity every turn and forces state through a hard external bottleneck (text/pixels only), isolating externalization from in-context tracking.

works.title: Gaia2: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Dynamic and Asynchronous Environments
works.what_it_does: 800+ verifiable mobile-environment scenarios testing agents under asynchronous, noisy, evolving conditions with tool use and multi-agent collaboration.
works.delta: Focuses on tool-use and ambiguity/adaptability under a live environment, not on a hard cross-turn memory bottleneck with fresh model instances or on certifying minimum survivable memory budgets.

works.title: EvoArena: Tracking Memory Evolution for Robust LLM Agents in Dynamic Environments
works.what_it_does: Introduces EvoMem, a patch-based memory paradigm recording structured update histories so agents can reason about environment changes over time (terminal/coding/social domains).
works.delta: Memory is a log of environment patches maintained by a continuing agent/harness; there is no fresh-instance-per-turn relay, no budget-constrained baton, and no image channel.

works.title: LoCoMo: Long-Term Conversational Memory Benchmark
works.venue_year: ACL 2024 (Maharana et al.), widely used through 2026
works.what_it_does: Multi-session (up to 32 sessions, ~600 turns) synthetic dialogues testing QA, summarization, and multimodal recall over weeks-to-months of simulated conversation.
works.delta: Tests recall inside a growing shared context/session log, not externalization across literal model resets; no compression-budget certification or hidden-state deduction task.

works.title: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
works.what_it_does: 766 multi-session tasks (web shopping, travel planning, search, formal reasoning) where agents must distill experience into memory and reuse it in later sessions; shows LoCoMo-saturated models perform poorly here.
works.delta: Sessions are agent-controlled memory writes reused by the *same* agent lineage across sessions; Relay's memory must survive a complete identity swap every single turn, with no session-level continuity at all.

works.title: MemGym: A Long-Horizon Memory Environment for LLM Agents
works.what_it_does: Five evaluation tracks (tool-use dialogue, deep research, coding, computer use) reporting 'memory-isolated' scores that decouple memory quality from reasoning/retrieval/tool-use confounders.
works.delta: Isolates memory as a scoring axis but within standard agentic tasks with a continuing agent; Relay isolates memory by architecture (mandatory identity reset + hard channel), a stronger and differently-motivated form of isolation, and adds a sound reference for certifying budgets.

works.title: Structured Belief State and the First Precision-Aware Benchmark for LLM Memory Retrieval (PrecisionMemBench / Tenure)
works.what_it_does: Argues existing memory benchmarks conflate answer-correctness with retrieval-correctness; introduces PrecisionMemBench (89 cases) and 'Tenure,' a structured belief-store proxy that resolves scope/retrieval before inference, hitting near-perfect retrieval passes vs. 0.05-0.08 precision baselines.
works.delta: Targets retrieval precision within a RAG-style belief store maintained by a harness across a session; Relay's 'sound reference' is a budget-matched, provably-sound *truncation* of a full belief tracker used to certify which fixed-size baton budgets are survivable at all, in a fresh-instance relay, not a retrieval-precision metric for a persistent store.

works.title: STALE: Can LLM Agents Know When Their Memories Are No Longer Valid?
works.what_it_does: 400 expert-validated conflict scenarios testing whether agents detect that an earlier stored memory has been implicitly invalidated by later evidence; best model reaches 55.2% accuracy.
works.delta: Studies belief revision/staleness detection over accumulated memory in one continuing agent; Relay never lets memory accumulate past one authored baton and does not study implicit contradiction detection as its central mechanic.

works.title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents
works.what_it_does: Lewis signaling game comparing five memory architectures (incl. stateless and persistent-notebook) across channel capacities; finds memory architecture predicts coordination success better than raw channel capacity, and notebooks let agents avoid high-capacity collapse.
works.delta: See threats — closest paper on the memory-architecture-vs-bottleneck axis, but a cooperative naming/coordination game, text-only, no sound-reference certification, no image channel, no constitutional-lock-in or write-render-read dissociation findings.

works.title: When Less Latent Leads to Better Relay: Information-Preserving Compression for Latent Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration
works.what_it_does: Compresses KV-cache latents relayed between LLM agents via Orthogonal BackFill, retaining ~10-20% of KV states while keeping 97-120% of full-relay accuracy across 9 math/QA/coding benchmarks.
works.delta: See threats — same 'relay under a budget' framing but the transmitted artifact is continuous latent state, not a human-legible text/image baton, so there's nothing to inspect for notation invention or drift, and no hidden-information deduction task.

works.title: Remember the Decision, Not the Description: A Rate-Distortion Framework for Agent Memory
works.what_it_does: Applies rate-distortion theory to agent-internal memory compression, proving conditions under which compressing to decision-relevant content preserves near-optimal policy performance under a budget.
works.delta: A theoretical framework for a single agent's self-compression, not an empirical benchmark; no fresh-instance relay, no image channel, no LLM-authored notation to analyze for drift or invented encodings.

works.title: Evolving Interpretable Constitutions for Multi-Agent Coordination
works.what_it_does: Uses LLM-guided evolutionary search to discover human-readable coordination rules ('constitutions') for grid-world resource-gathering agents; evolved constitutions beat one-shot LLM-designed ones and discover that minimizing communication outperforms verbose coordination.
works.delta: See threats — same qualitative shape (self-authored governance underperforms an alternative) but in a resource-survival game with iteratively-evolved (not experimenter-imposed) rules, no per-turn identity reset, no character/pixel transmission budget.

works.title: Age of LLM: A Strategic 1v1 Benchmark for Reasoning, Diplomacy and Reliability of LLMs under Fog of War
works.what_it_does: Turn-based 1v1 wargame with fog of war and diplomacy; treats the illegal-action rate (~58% of which are fog/state errors) as a proxy for belief-tracking quality across 15 models and 54 matches.
works.delta: Each side is a single continuing agent maintaining its own belief state privately in-context; there is no forced externalization through a fresh instance each turn, no fixed transmission budget, and no certified-sound reference tracker.

works.title: MastermindEval: A Simple But Scalable Reasoning Benchmark
works.what_it_does: LLM-as-codebreaker in classic Mastermind, varying code length/symbols/guess budget to probe deductive reasoning from peg-color/position feedback.
works.delta: Single continuing agent reasons over full visible transcript within one context; no cross-instance relay, no compression baton, no image channel, no certification of survivable memory budgets.

works.title: Externalization in LLM Agents: A Unified Review of Memory, Skills, Protocols and Harness Engineering
works.what_it_does: Survey/taxonomy arguing agent capability increasingly lives in the surrounding harness (memory stores, skills, protocols) rather than the model itself; frames memory as externalizing state across time.
works.delta: A conceptual review, not an experimental benchmark; provides useful framing language ('externalization') but no fresh-instance relay design, no games, no budget certification, no empirical findings about notation drift or constitutional lock-in.

works.title: Evaluating Memory in LLM Agents via Incremental Multi-Turn Interactions (MemoryAgentBench)
works.what_it_does: Benchmark spanning four competencies (accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, conflict resolution) for memory-augmented agents across incremental multi-turn tasks.
works.delta: Agent persists and accumulates memory turn over turn within its own run; Relay's defining constraint (a new, contextless model instance every single turn) is absent, as is any image/pixel channel or sound-reference certification.

works.title: WorldLines: Benchmarking and Modeling Long-Horizon Stateful Embodied Agents
works.what_it_does: Embodied long-horizon benchmark modeling agent state persistence and world dynamics over extended stateful trajectories.
works.delta: Embodied/simulated-world setting with a continuing agent tracking physical state; no textual/image bottleneck baton, no fresh-instance-per-turn design, no deduction-game framing.

works.title: Self-Programmed Execution for Language-Model Agents ('Telephone' relay game)
works.what_it_does: Includes a 'Telephone' orchestration test where a message is passed through 8 relays; a fresh LLM instance receives the prior relay's output and rewrites it, testing meaning-preservation through stateless hand-offs.
works.delta: Closest prior example of a literal fresh-instance-per-turn relay chain, but the task is open-ended paraphrase/meaning-preservation of a single sentence, not a hidden-information deduction game with a verifiable ground-truth board state, no fixed character/pixel budget being stress-tested, and no sound-reference certification of survivable compression.

phrases: Where prompt-compression work (LLMLingua, gisting, AutoCompressors, ICAE) measures how much of a static document survives a compression ratio, Blindboard: Relay measures whether a hidden, evolving belief state survives compression when the only continuity across turns is a budget-capped baton read by a brand-new model instance — compression quality is scored by downstream deduction success, not perplexity or ROUGE against the source.

Unlike 'broken telephone' degradation studies (ACL 2025) that regenerate free-form translations/paraphrases with no size constraint and no ground truth beyond the original text, Relay imposes a hard character/pixel budget and certifies exactly which budgets are survivable via a budget-matched sound reference (a belief tracker serialized through the identical bottleneck with provably-sound truncation) — so degradation is measured against an information-theoretic floor, not just against a prior draft.

Signaling-game work ('From Signals to Structure') shows persistent notebooks beat stateless agents when two continuing agents invent a shared code with no hidden state to track; Relay shows a comparable externalization gap inside a certified hidden-state deduction task, then adds findings a coordination game structurally cannot produce: constitutional lock-in (self-designed pinned specs underperform adaptive notation) and per-model crossover under imposed schema (the smallest model beats its own full-transcript score) rather than a smooth capability gradient.

BabelTele shows LLMs can compress static text to roughly a quarter of its length at high fidelity when asked to; Relay is the first to show a flagship model spontaneously inventing a comparably dense positional-string encoding unprompted, mid-game, purely as a side effect of trying to win under a hard budget, and to certify that its self-invented codec tracks the provably-sound reference floor.

No prior compression-memory study spans both a text bottleneck and a pixel bottleneck for the same underlying task and finds that write-render-read fidelity and downstream game performance dissociate, or that models default to writing literal text inside rendered images rather than exploiting spatial/2D encoding — a negative result the optical-memory efficiency systems (AgentOCR, OCR-Memory, ScrapMem) aren't built to surface since they optimize token savings on real agent trajectories, not diagnose whether models discover visual encoding on their own.

works.title: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models
works.what_it_does: Coarse-to-fine prompt compression: a budget controller allocates compression ratios across prompt components, then iterative token-level compression removes low-information tokens while preserving conditional dependencies, aligned to the target LLM's distribution.
works.delta: Compresses a static, given prompt for inference efficiency (measured by task accuracy retention and latency); Relay compresses an evolving hidden belief state passed between fresh model instances across a multi-turn game and scores it by whether deduction/game success survives, with a certified sound-baseline floor LLMLingua has no analogue of.

works.title: LongLLMLingua: Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression
works.what_it_does: Extends LLMLingua with question-aware coarse-to-fine compression and a document reordering mechanism for long-context QA, showing compression can even improve downstream accuracy by reducing 'lost in the middle' noise.
works.delta: Single-shot compression of a long context for one query; no repeated compress-decompress cycle across turns/instances, no notion of a hard bottleneck a fresh reader must fully reconstruct state from, and no drift/mutation of an encoding over successive generations as in Relay's notation-drift finding.

works.title: LLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression
works.what_it_does: Trains a smaller token-classification model via data distillation to do task-agnostic prompt compression, improving faithfulness and out-of-domain generalization over the original LLMLingua's perplexity-based token dropping.
works.delta: A trained, purpose-built compressor model applied to static prompts; Relay studies compression as an emergent, self-directed behavior of the same general-purpose model under game pressure, with no separate compressor network and no fixed compression target ratio — the model chooses its own encoding under a hard budget.

works.title: Learning to Compress Prompts with Gist Tokens
works.what_it_does: Fine-tunes an LM to compress prompts into a handful of learned 'gist' continuous-vector tokens via modified attention masking, achieving up to 26x compression with minimal quality loss and cacheable/reusable gists.
works.delta: Soft, sub-symbolic compression baked into model weights via training; Relay's baton is either plain human-legible text under a character budget or a literal rendered image, produced zero-shot by an unmodified model and read by a different fresh instance, making the compression strategy itself an observable, evolving artifact rather than a fixed learned vector.

works.title: Adapting Language Models to Compress Contexts (AutoCompressors)
works.what_it_does: Fine-tunes LMs to recursively compress long contexts into 'summary vectors' usable as soft prompts, extending effective context to tens of thousands of tokens with improved perplexity and retrieval-augmentation utility.
works.delta: Targets perplexity/language-modeling quality over long documents via trained recursive vector summarization; Relay targets whether a hidden game-relevant belief state survives a hard bottleneck across independently-instantiated readers, evaluated by task success and certified against an information-theoretic sound baseline, not perplexity.

works.title: In-context Autoencoder (ICAE) for Context Compression in a Large Language Model
works.what_it_does: Trains an LLM-based encoder to compress long context into a small number of memory slot representations that a (possibly frozen) target LLM decodes from, autoencoder-style, for context-length reduction.
works.delta: Single encode/decode pass optimized for reconstruction/downstream QA; Relay chains many independent compress-then-reconstruct hops across turns and fresh instances in a game, and specifically studies how the encoding scheme itself changes (notation drift) across that chain, which a one-shot autoencoder setup cannot exhibit.

works.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
works.what_it_does: Builds a hierarchical tree of recursive summaries via bottom-up clustering and abstraction over document chunks, then retrieves across abstraction levels for long-document QA.
works.delta: Recursive summarization here builds a static retrieval index over a fixed corpus for QA; Relay's 'recursive summarization' is a live, adversarial-to-forgetting relay where each summary is the only surviving trace of state for a fresh reader in an ongoing deduction game, with certified budget floors RAPTOR doesn't define.

works.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
works.what_it_does: Proposes an OS-inspired virtual context management scheme where the LLM manages its own paging between limited main-context and larger external/archival storage, self-editing what it keeps in-context.
works.delta: A single continuing agent manages its own memory hierarchy over one long session; Relay's memory holder is never the same instance twice — every turn is a fresh model with zero conversation history, so 'memory' exists only in the externalized baton, isolating externalization as its own capability rather than in-context self-management.

works.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
works.what_it_does: Simulated agents maintain a memory stream of observations, periodically reflect to generate higher-level summaries, and retrieve by recency/importance/relevance to drive believable behavior in a sandbox town.
works.delta: Memory reflection/summarization here serves open-ended believability, not a scoreable ground-truth task, and the same agent persists across the whole simulation; Relay isolates a certified, gradeable hidden-state tracking task specifically to measure information loss through a hard bottleneck with no persistent agent identity.

works.title: Recursively Summarizing Books with Human Feedback
works.what_it_does: Trains models via human feedback to summarize book chunks and then recursively summarize summaries-of-summaries to compress entire books, using recursive decomposition to sidestep length limits.
works.delta: An early, human-feedback-trained instance of recursive summarization for static narrative compression, evaluated by human judgment of summary quality; Relay uses no training/feedback loop at all (fully zero-shot, off-the-shelf models), targets a dynamic hidden game state rather than a fixed book, and grades against a certified sound reference rather than human preference.

works.title: LLM as a Broken Telephone: Iterative Generation Distorts Information
works.what_it_does: Runs iterative translation/paraphrase chains (e.g., repeated round-trip translation) across up to 100 fresh model calls, each seeing only the prior output, and measures progressive factual/semantic distortion via BLEU/ROUGE/FActScore; finds distortion is unavoidable but modulated by language choice and temperature.
works.delta: No compression pressure at all — outputs are capped only by a generous 8000-token ceiling, so there is no hard bottleneck forcing lossy encoding, no certified/sound baseline for how much should survive, and no study of self-invented notation; it studies drift in natural-language semantics under free regeneration, whereas Relay studies drift in a self-invented compressed code under a hard, game-relevant budget.

works.title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents
works.what_it_does: In a Lewis signaling game, compares five memory architectures (including stateless vs. persistent-private-notebook agents) across channel capacities; finds memory architecture predicts stable coordination better than channel capacity, and notebooks let agents externalize conventions instead of re-deriving them each round.
works.delta: A pure sender/receiver coordination game with no hidden state to deduce, no character/pixel budget on the notebook, and no certified-optimal reference for what a memory system should preserve; Relay embeds the same externalization-vs-statelessness contrast inside a certified hidden-state deduction task and additionally finds a per-model crossover effect and constitutional lock-in that a coordination-only setup cannot produce.

works.title: Large Language Models Do Not Always Need Readable Language (BabelTele)
works.what_it_does: Probes LLMs' capacity to generate and interpret dense, non-human-readable textual representations ('BabelTele') that trade readability for information density, evaluating via readability diagnostics, likelihood, human ratings, downstream tasks, cross-model transfer, agent memory, and multi-agent communication; reports 99.5% semantic fidelity at 27.9% of original length.
works.delta: BabelTele representations appear to be elicited/probed as a deliberate representational paradigm the researchers study directly, on static text/QA content; Relay's flagship-model dense encoding arises unprompted as a side effect of playing a hidden-state deduction game under a hard budget, and is graded not by fidelity/likelihood but by whether it beats a provably-sound reference codec on game outcomes.

works.title: LLM Agents Are Latent Context Managers: Eliciting Self-Managed Context via a Proprioceptive Dashboard (VISTA)
works.what_it_does: Gives a single continuing agent visibility into its own working-memory state (per-block token usage, recency, access history) rather than imposing a compression policy, and shows this training-free 'dashboard' substantially improves long-horizon task performance across benchmarks like LOCA-Bench.
works.delta: Argues self-directed context management (given the right visibility) works well for a single persisting agent; Relay's fresh-instance-per-turn design removes persistence entirely and specifically finds the opposite pattern for self-designed schemes — a self-authored pinned spec becomes a lock-in liability across generations rather than a benefit, a contrast VISTA's continuing-agent setup can't test.

works.title: MemAgent: Reshaping Long-Context LLM with Multi-Conv RL-based Memory Agent
works.what_it_does: RL-trains a model to read documents in chunks and overwrite a fixed-length token memory after each chunk, extrapolating from 8K-token training to 3.5M-token QA with under 5% performance loss.
works.delta: A trained overwrite policy for one continuing model processing a static document sequentially; Relay uses no training at all, hands the memory to a genuinely different model instance each turn, and evaluates a dynamic adversarial-to-forgetting deduction game rather than long-document QA extrapolation.

works.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
works.what_it_does: RL-trains long-horizon coding/tool-use agents to keep performing well after their trajectory is compacted into a summary once context limits are hit, jointly optimizing task success and summary generation via token-level loss normalization.
works.delta: Optimizes a trained policy for one continuing agent's occasional compaction events inside real coding/tool tasks (e.g., SWE-bench); Relay uses zero-shot models, compacts on every single turn rather than only near a context limit, and certifies survivable budgets against a sound reference rather than measuring benchmark pass-rate lift from RL training.

works.title: AgentOCR: Reimagining Agent History via Optical Self-Compression
works.what_it_does: RL-trains an agent to render its own interaction history as cached images instead of text, letting it choose a compression rate under a compression-aware reward; reports >95% task performance retention on ALFWorld/search QA with >50% token reduction.
works.delta: An RL-trained efficiency system for one continuing agent's own trajectory, optimizing token cost on real embodied/QA tasks; Relay's pixel channel is a zero-shot diagnostic probe across fresh instances specifically asking whether models exploit 2D spatial encoding at all (finding: they don't, they write text into the image) and whether render fidelity tracks game performance (finding: it doesn't) — questions an efficiency-optimized system isn't built to surface.

works.title: ClawVM: Harness-Managed Virtual Memory for Stateful Tool-Using LLM Agents
works.what_it_does: A systems-layer virtual memory manager for agent harnesses that enforces typed pages, minimum-fidelity invariants, and validated writeback at compaction/reset boundaries to eliminate reliability faults (lost state, destructive writes) under a token budget.
works.delta: Solves engineering reliability of memory operations (no lost/corrupted state) for production tool-agents, not information-theoretic compressibility of a hidden belief state; Relay isn't concerned with whether writeback is faithfully executed by the harness but with what a model chooses to write and whether that choice preserves enough signal to win a certified deduction game.

threats.title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents
threats.overlap: Directly compares stateless agents to agents with a persistent private notebook across memory architectures and finds memory architecture (not raw channel capacity) determines whether interaction history becomes a stable, externalized convention — the same 'externalization is a distinct, load-bearing capability' thesis Relay argues, and both use a small-vocabulary/symbol-budget framing reminiscent of a character budget.
threats.differentiation: It is a Lewis signaling/coordination game with no hidden state to deduce — success means two roles agree on arbitrary labels for known objects, not that a reader reconstructs a concealed board state. There is no hard character/pixel budget with a provably-sound reference baseline (their 'channel capacity' is vocabulary size, with only an information-bottleneck-style capacity heuristic as an informal target, not a certified truncation-soundness proof). No notation-drift-across-generations analysis, no self-designed-spec lock-in finding, no per-model crossover under imposed schema, and no image/pixel channel.
threats.claims_to_verify: Confirm (from the full paper, not abstract) whether the 'stateless' vs. 'notebook' roles are literally instantiated as fresh model calls each round with the notebook as the only carried artifact (architecturally close to Relay's baton), or whether some conversational memory persists outside the notebook; confirm there is no formal soundness/optimality certificate for the notebook's capacity beyond the informal 'capacity = object count' heuristic; confirm the five memory architectures don't already include an imposed-schema-vs-self-designed-schema contrast that would preempt Relay's constitutional-lock-in finding.

threats.title: Large Language Models Do Not Always Need Readable Language (BabelTele)
threats.overlap: Directly studies LLMs producing and consuming dense, non-standard, information-rich textual representations that sacrifice human readability for compression, including agent-memory and multi-agent-communication evaluation settings — the same phenomenon Relay reports when its flagship model spontaneously invents a denser-than-reference positional-string encoding.
threats.differentiation: BabelTele is framed and evaluated as a representational paradigm the researchers probe/elicit directly (via readability diagnostics, likelihood, human questionnaires) on general text and downstream tasks; it is not shown to emerge unprompted as a side effect of trying to win a hidden-state deduction game under a hard turn-by-turn budget passed between fresh instances, and it is not benchmarked against a provably-sound reference tracker or graded by whether it beats a certified information floor — it's graded by fidelity/readability/likelihood metrics, not game-theoretic outcome.
threats.claims_to_verify: Read the full paper (not abstract) to determine whether any BabelTele emergence is spontaneous/unprompted by a specific model in an agentic task, or whether it is elicited by an explicit compression instruction/training signal; check whether the 'agent memory' and 'multi-agent communication' evaluations involve any hidden ground-truth state a receiver must reconstruct (vs. shared/known information), and whether any budget in that setting is certified against a sound baseline the way Relay's is.

threats.title: LLM as a Broken Telephone: Iterative Generation Distorts Information
threats.overlap: Studies information distortion across chains of iterative generation where each step is a fresh model call seeing only the immediately prior output — architecturally close to Relay's fresh-instance-per-turn relay — and frames the core phenomenon as progressive, unavoidable degradation, the same lineage as Relay's notation-drift finding (models mutating their own notation across generations).
threats.differentiation: Confirmed via direct methodology check: there is no hard length/character budget forcing compression at all (generation is capped at a generous 8000 tokens 'to encourage open-ended generation'), so there's no bottleneck pressure driving lossy encoding; there is no certified/sound reference baseline for expected information survival (only empirical BLEU/ROUGE/FActScore drift vs. the original); and the paper explicitly does not address models inventing notation/symbolic shorthand — it's semantic/factual drift in ordinary natural-language paraphrase and translation, not drift in a self-invented compressed code under budget pressure.
threats.claims_to_verify: This was verified directly against the paper's methodology (fetched arXiv HTML): confirm no hard compression constraint, fresh-call-per-iteration structure, translation/rephrasing/multilingual chain task types, absence of a certified baseline, and absence of any notation-invention discussion — these should be re-checked against the final ACL camera-ready in case of revisions, but the arXiv HTML version supports all five differentiation points above.

phrases: Unlike population-scale naming games or advice-passing chains where agents keep rolling context or many-round memory, Blindboard: Relay enforces true amnesia: every turn is a categorically fresh model instance whose only link to the past is one authored artifact under a hard budget.

Where prior LLM telephone-game and iterated-learning studies report drift or degeneration empirically, Relay certifies it: a budget-matched sound reference (a belief tracker serialized through the identical bottleneck, with provably-sound truncation) tells us which budgets are information-theoretically survivable, separating genuine drift from an insufficient budget.

Our notation-drift finding — a single model inventing, then mutating, its own encoding scheme across amnesiac generations within one episode — isolates the iterated-learning transmission bottleneck at the smallest possible unit: one model, one episode, no population, no gradient updates, and no cross-agent negotiation.

Running the identical relay through a text baton and a rendered-image baton lets Relay show, apparently for the first time, that write-render-read fidelity and downstream task performance dissociate in the pixel channel, and that no tested model spontaneously uses spatial encoding even when it would out-compress text.

Memory scaffolding in Relay produces per-model crossover, not a uniform capability gradient — an imposed schema that lets the smallest model beat its own full-transcript score can be neutral or harmful for larger models — a result classic iterated-learning bottleneck theory does not predict and that population-scale convention-formation studies, operating at a different unit of analysis, have not reported.

works.title: Spontaneous evolution of linguistic structure: an iterated learning model of the emergence of regularity and irregularity
works.what_it_does: Founding iterated learning model (ILM): shows a transmission bottleneck (learners see only a subset of the prior generation's language) creates pressure for compositional structure over generations of symbolic learners.
works.delta: Relay borrows the transmission-bottleneck logic but replaces the corpus-subset bottleneck with a hard character/pixel budget on a single artifact, and studies one LLM relaying to itself within one episode rather than a population of symbolic learners across many generations.

works.title: Iterated Learning: A Framework for the Emergence of Language
works.what_it_does: Formalizes iterated learning as a framework where each learner's output becomes the next learner's input, establishing the paradigm used by nearly all later language-evolution simulations.
works.delta: Relay adopts the same generational-transmission chain structure but instruments it as an LLM capability benchmark with a certified survivable-budget floor, not a model of human language evolution.

works.title: Iterated learning and the evolution of language
works.venue_year: Current Opinion in Neurobiology, 2014 (Kirby, Griffiths & Smith)
works.what_it_does: Review showing iterated learning turns an unstructured proto-language into a stable, compositional communication system purely from the bottleneck plus learner biases, no communicative pressure required.
works.delta: Relay's notation drift shows the opposite trajectory in one respect: a mid-tier model's self-invented notation degrades/mutates rather than stabilizing, because there is no population averaging out idiosyncratic learner bias across many independent chains.

works.title: Compositional languages emerge in a neural iterated learning model
works.what_it_does: First neural-network instantiation of the ILM bottleneck; shows an explicit generational imitation-then-interaction loop with neural agents produces compositional emergent language, unlike single-generation reinforcement learning.
works.delta: Relay's baton mechanism is a text/image bottleneck rather than a training bottleneck, and it operates on a single frozen LLM's zero-shot behavior across amnesiac calls rather than on trained neural nets updated generation to generation.

works.title: Countering Language Drift with Seeded Iterated Learning
works.what_it_does: Diagnoses 'language drift' when RL-tuned neural agents optimize a non-linguistic reward and their protocol diverges from natural language, then uses iterated learning (seeded with human data) to counter it.
works.delta: Relay's notation drift is drift in a self-invented (not natural-language-seeded) code under a hard channel budget, observed in inference-time LLM generations rather than RL fine-tuning steps, with no corrective seeding mechanism to counter it.

works.title: Compositionality and Generalization in Emergent Languages
works.what_it_does: Shows compositional emergent languages are easier for new listeners to learn (ease-of-transmission advantage) but compositionality does not by itself guarantee better task generalization.
works.delta: Relay measures whether a single model's invented notation is even stable across its own amnesiac generations, a prerequisite question that precedes Chaabouni et al.'s learnability-vs-generalization question.

works.title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data
works.venue_year: Nature 631, 2024 (Shumailov et al.; preprint 'Curse of Recursion')
works.what_it_does: Shows models trained recursively on their own generated data suffer 'model collapse': progressive loss of distributional tails and drift toward degenerate central tendencies across training generations.
works.delta: Relay's degeneration happens within a single inference episode via context truncation, not across training runs via gradient updates on synthetic data; it is a generational-transmission relative of model collapse rather than an instance of it.

works.title: Learning to solve complex tasks by growing knowledge culturally across generations
works.venue_year: arXiv 2021 (Colas, Karch, Kovac, Oudeyer et al.)
works.what_it_does: RL agents accumulate and pass on knowledge (goals, skills) across successive artificial 'generations' of learners in an open-ended environment, showing cultural accumulation outperforms any single generation.
works.delta: Relay's generations are amnesiac LLM calls within one game episode passing a budgeted note, not RL policies passing accumulated skill libraries across a long-horizon curriculum.

works.title: Language and Experience: A Computational Model of Social Learning in Complex Tasks
works.venue_year: ICLR 2026 / CogSci 2025 (Colas, Mills, Prystawski, Tessler, Goodman, Andreas, Tenenbaum)
works.what_it_does: Models social learning as Bayesian inference over sensorimotor and linguistic data: agents play a game for a limited number of 'lives,' then write advice consumed by the next generation, iterated across generations and ten video games, fit to human behavioral data.
works.delta: Relay shares the fresh-learner-plus-written-note generational structure but adds a hard budget with a certified sound-reference floor, tests a hidden-state deduction game rather than exploration/advice efficacy, and asks about self-invented notation stability rather than whether advice speeds learning.

works.title: When LLMs Play the Telephone Game: Cumulative Changes and Attractors in Iterated Cultural Transmissions
works.what_it_does: Chains LLM agents in rephrase/inspire/continue tasks and tracks toxicity, positivity, reading difficulty, and length, finding model-specific 'attractor' states chains converge to, strongest under open-ended instructions.
works.delta: Relay's chain passes a task-critical state artifact under a hard budget in a verifiable deduction game (correctness is checkable against ground truth) rather than free-text style properties (toxicity, positivity) with no ground-truth target.

works.title: LLM as a Broken Telephone: Iterative Generation Distorts Information
works.what_it_does: Shows iterative generation (e.g., translation/paraphrase relay across languages or models) compounds distortion, and that longer or more heterogeneous chains amplify information loss, sometimes triggering collapse-like dynamics.
works.delta: Relay's distortion is measured against a certified survivable-budget floor and a checkable game state, not against a diffuse notion of 'information fidelity' in translated/paraphrased text with no ground truth.

works.title: Shaping Shared Languages: Human and Large Language Models' Inductive Biases in Emergent Communication
works.what_it_does: Runs LLMs (and humans) in an iterated referential game with generational transmission; initially holistic emergent languages acquire compositional structure across generations but LLM-optimized languages become less diverse/more degenerate than human-optimized ones.
works.delta: Relay studies one model relaying to itself within a single episode (no separate population of learners per generation) and measures notation stability/mutation directly rather than compositionality-vs-diversity trade-offs across a trained population.

works.title: Searching for Structure: Investigating Emergent Communication with Large Language Models
works.what_it_does: LLM sender/receiver pairs (Llama-3-70B) develop an artificial language across communication rounds and iterated-learning generations; finds structure (TopSim) increases but later generations show degenerate many-to-one signal-attribute mappings.
works.delta: Relay isolates the phenomenon to a single model's own within-episode notation (not a sender/receiver pair building shared vocabulary across many interactive rounds) and certifies degeneration against a sound-reference budget floor rather than measuring TopSim/n-gram statistics alone.

works.title: Emergent Social Conventions and Collective Bias in LLM Populations
works.what_it_does: Populations of 24-200 LLM agents playing a pairwise naming game spontaneously converge on shared conventions from local interactions alone, and can exhibit strong collective bias absent in any individual agent; committed minorities can tip the population.
works.delta: Relay has no population and no tipping dynamics; it asks whether a single model's own convention survives its own amnesiac hand-offs within one episode, a within-agent stability question orthogonal to their between-agent population question.

works.title: Exploring the Topology and Memory of Consensus: How LLM Agents Agree, Fragment, or Settle When Forming Conventions
works.what_it_does: 432 runs of a networked naming game across 8 fixed 16-agent topologies show memory depth and network topology jointly and sometimes oppositely determine whether populations converge, fragment, or reach consensus quickly.
works.delta: Relay's 'memory' is a single hard-budgeted authored artifact carried by amnesiac successors in a linear chain, not a rolling multi-round history window inside a many-agent network topology.

works.title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents
works.what_it_does: Two-agent Lewis signaling game where each round is a fresh LLM call; compares a persistent notebook (≤150 words) and fixed-slot codebook (10 slots) against stateless rolling-context agents, finding notebook memory gives most reliable coordination and documenting 'convention drift' where the sender re-assigns a token sequence to a different object mid-run, degrading the receiver's accumulated mapping.
works.delta: Closest known prior art to our core mechanism (fresh-call generations plus a budgeted externalized artifact producing convention/notation drift); Relay differs by testing a state-tracking deduction game (not object-naming), adding a certified sound-reference floor across systematically varied budgets, comparing across many frontier models rather than one architecture ablation, and adding a second (pixel/image) channel that this paper does not test.

works.title: Model Collapse as Cultural Evolution
works.what_it_does: Reframes model collapse in terms of cultural-evolution theory; trains LLaMA-2-7B/Mistral-7B recursively for 10 generations across three languages, finding compositionality rises then falls (non-monotonic) under unfiltered self-training, matching human transmission-chain regularization patterns (R²=0.94).
works.delta: Relay's generations are inference-time amnesiac calls within a single episode with a hard externalization budget, not recursive fine-tuning generations over a training corpus; no gradient updates or corpus-level statistics are involved.

works.title: SIGN: Schema-Induced Games for Naming
works.what_it_does: Compares schema-induced (structured) communication against unconstrained natural-language naming-game communication, finding schema-induced convention formation converges faster with up to 5.8x higher agreement.
works.delta: Relay's imposed-schema finding is per-model and crossover (helps the smallest model, not larger ones) within a single amnesiac relay chain, whereas SIGN reports an average schema-vs-free-form effect across a multi-agent naming-game population without characterizing per-model heterogeneity.

threats.title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents
threats.overlap: Uses the same core mechanism we thought was novel: every round is a fresh LLM API call, memory only persists via an explicit, size-bounded authored artifact (a ≤150-word notebook or 10-slot codebook) re-injected into the next call, and they explicitly document 'convention drift' — the sender re-assigning an established token sequence to a different object mid-run, degrading the receiver's accumulated mapping — which is essentially our notation-drift finding in a different game.
threats.differentiation: Their game is object naming/reference (Lewis signaling game); ours is hidden-state deduction requiring the baton to encode and update a belief state, a harder and more state-ful transmission target. They test one architecture ablation (notebook vs. codebook vs. stateless) on presumably one model; we certify survivable budgets with a provably-sound truncated-belief-tracker reference and compare across many frontier models to show per-model divergence (small models write plans not state; the flagship invents a denser-than-reference codec). We also run a second, pixel/image channel (rendered SVG baton) and find a fidelity/performance dissociation absent from their text-only design.
threats.claims_to_verify: Confirm whether their 'fresh LLM API call' constitutes true zero-context amnesia (no hidden system-level continuity) versus ours; confirm how many distinct models they test (their summary suggests architecture variation more than model variation) and whether they report any per-model capability gradient or crossover comparable to our imposed-schema effect; confirm whether they impose any theoretically-grounded sound/optimal baseline for the 150-word or 10-slot budget, or only empirical cross-architecture comparison; confirm publication status/date (arXiv 2607.00233, dated July 2026) relative to our own release timeline.

threats.title: Language and Experience: A Computational Model of Social Learning in Complex Tasks
threats.overlap: Structurally near-identical scaffold to our relay: an agent plays a game for a limited number of 'lives,' then writes advice/text that is the sole input the next generation receives, iterated across generations and multiple game environments — i.e., fresh-learner-plus-written-note generational transmission, matched against human behavioral data.
threats.differentiation: Their framing is social learning / advice efficacy modeled via Bayesian inference and validated against human data, not a benchmark of LLM notation stability or capability under a hard externalization budget. We could not confirm they impose any explicit character/token/pixel budget on the advice, use a certified sound-reference floor, study self-invented notation/encoding stability, or compare a text vs. image transmission channel — all central to our contribution.
threats.claims_to_verify: Verify whether advice length is unconstrained or budget-limited in their design; verify whether 'agents' across generations are literally fresh LLM calls with zero shared context or whether the modeling agent (the Bayesian inference engine) itself persists across generations while only the in-game character resets; verify whether they test multiple frontier LLMs and report per-model differences, or center the paper on fitting one model class to human data; verify the exact number of 'lives' and generations and whether any game involves hidden-state deduction akin to ours.

threats.title: Emergent Social Conventions and Collective Bias in LLM Populations (companion: Exploring the Topology and Memory of Consensus)
threats.overlap: Directly studies how memory (depth/window) affects convention stability and formation among LLM agents, the closest existing empirical treatment of 'convention stability' as a function of memory design, which is the question our within-episode notation-drift finding also targets.
threats.differentiation: These are population-scale (16-200 agents), many-round social-convention games where each agent is a persistent instance retaining a rolling memory window across many pairwise interactions, not a single linear chain of amnesiac successors within one bounded episode. There is no hard externalization budget forcing compression into a single authored artifact, and no certified sound-reference floor; the object of study is population-level consensus/fragmentation and collective bias, not a single model's own encoding surviving its own hand-offs.
threats.claims_to_verify: Verify whether 'memory depth' in these papers means a rolling window of raw conversational transcript (uncompressed) versus our hard-budgeted authored artifact; verify whether any individual-agent (not population-level) drift/mutation of an invented naming convention is reported, which would be the most direct precedent for our within-episode single-model notation-drift claim; verify exact population sizes, round counts, and whether any image/pixel channel variant exists in follow-up work.

phrases: Blindboard: Relay is, to our knowledge, the first benchmark to certify which text/pixel baton budgets are survivable by pairing every budget against a provably-sound serialized belief-tracker floor, rather than only measuring empirical degradation.

Unlike self-note and handoff literature built around one persistent agent notating for its own future turns (Reflexion, Self-Notes, MemGPT, sleep-time compute, ExpeL), Blindboard: Relay severs identity completely every turn — a fresh, independently-sampled instance receives nothing but the baton, with no shared weights, session, or memory beyond it.

Where Self-Spec finds that letting a model design its own structuring artifact modestly helps single-shot code generation, Blindboard: Relay shows the opposite over a long relay: a self-designed, pinned notation degrades into constitutional lock-in, while an imposed external schema can flip the ranking and let the smallest model beat its own unconstrained full-transcript score.

Blindboard: Relay extends telephone-game and agent-drift style degradation studies with a controlled, budget-matched design and a sound-reference certification, letting it isolate how much observed drift is capability-limited versus budget-limited rather than reporting degradation alone.

Through its pixel-channel condition, Blindboard: Relay is (to our knowledge) the first study to show that LLMs given a free canvas for cross-instance memory default to writing text inside the image rather than inventing a spatial/graphical encoding, and to separately measure write-render-read fidelity from downstream game performance.

works.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
works.what_it_does: A single persistent agent converts environmental/task feedback into first-person natural-language reflections, stored in an explicit episodic memory buffer, to improve its own performance on repeated attempts at the same task.
works.delta: The reflecting and the acting are done by the same continuing agent across trials of one task; there is no hard external budget on the note, no fresh independently-sampled instance per turn, and no certified sound-reference floor to calibrate what is survivable.

works.title: Learning to Reason and Memorize with Self-Notes
works.what_it_does: Lets a model interleave free-form 'self-notes' into its own input context at any point during a single continuous generation, functioning as an on-the-fly scratchpad plus working memory that outperforms chain-of-thought/scratchpad baselines.
works.delta: Notes live inside one uninterrupted generation by one instance; there is no cross-instance handoff, no hard character/pixel budget forcing compression, and no relay of many independently-sampled models.

works.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
works.what_it_does: Gives simulated agents an append-only natural-language memory stream plus periodic reflection and retrieval, letting the same persistent agent identity plan and act believably over simulated days.
works.delta: Memory is an unbounded, retrieval-augmented log maintained by one continuing agent, not a hard-budgeted baton passed between literally fresh instances with no other shared state.

works.title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
works.what_it_does: Extracts generalizable natural-language insights from a pool of past successful/failed trajectories (built partly via Reflexion) into an experience library reused across many different downstream tasks, without gradient updates.
works.delta: Insights are cross-task, cumulative, and unbounded in size; the benchmark has no single continuous deduction game, no per-turn character/pixel budget, and no fresh-instance-per-turn structure.

works.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
works.what_it_does: Builds an ever-growing library of executable-code skills in Minecraft, retrieved by embedding similarity and reused across a lifelong, open-ended curriculum.
works.delta: The carried artifact is reusable code, not a compressed natural-language/image state note; there is no hard bottleneck budget and no relay of independent fresh instances turn-by-turn.

works.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
works.what_it_does: Introduces OS-style virtual context management, paging information between a bounded main context and unbounded archival/recall storage via the agent's own function calls, for one continuing agent across long or multi-session interactions.
works.delta: The same agent manages its own paging over an effectively unbounded external store; there is no certified hard budget forcing everything through a single note/image, and no relay across independently-sampled fresh instances.

works.title: Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
works.what_it_does: Has the model 'think' offline about a context during idle time, precomputing useful intermediate quantities before a query arrives, cutting test-time compute needed for the same accuracy.
works.delta: The precomputed state is prepared before the query by (implicitly) the same model/context, not authored under a hard bottleneck and then handed to a genuinely fresh, independently-sampled instance turn by turn.

works.title: Chain of Agents: Large Language Models Collaborating on Long-Context Tasks
works.what_it_does: Worker agents sequentially read segments of a long document and pass natural-language summaries forward to the next worker, with a final manager agent synthesizing the chain's outputs for QA/summarization/code tasks.
works.delta: This is a genuine relay/baton structure, but for long-document comprehension rather than a hidden-information deduction game; there is no hard character/pixel budget certified against a sound-reference floor, and no analysis of notation invention or drift.

works.title: MEM1: Learning to Synergize Memory and Reasoning for Efficient Long-Horizon Agents
works.what_it_does: Trains, via end-to-end RL, a policy that updates a single compact internal state each turn, jointly consolidating memory and reasoning while discarding irrelevant information, achieving constant memory across long multi-turn tasks.
works.delta: The state-writer is a trained, weight-persistent policy reused every turn, not a zero-shot fresh instance; there is no certified sound-reference floor and no character/pixel hard-budget framing.

works.title: LLM as a Broken Telephone: Iterative Generation Distorts Information
works.what_it_does: Runs long chains of iterative regeneration (e.g., repeated translation) and quantifies how factual and semantic content distorts over up to 100 iterations, testing mitigations like low temperature and explicit preservation instructions.
works.delta: Chains are unconstrained-length natural-language regenerations without a hard character/pixel budget or notation-invention analysis, and use no sound-reference floor to certify which regimes are survivable; unclear whether hops are genuinely independent fresh instances versus the same model re-prompted.

works.title: Agent Drift: Quantifying Behavioral Degradation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems Over Extended Interactions
works.what_it_does: Proposes an Agent Stability Index across 12 dimensions to quantify semantic, coordination, and behavioral drift in multi-agent systems over extended interactions, based on 800+ simulated workflows.
works.delta: A general, correlational measure of degradation across varied multi-agent workflows, not a controlled single-relay design with a hard baton budget, notation-invention analysis, or a certified sound-reference floor.

works.title: Self-Spec: Model-Authored Specifications for Reliable LLM Code Generation
works.what_it_does: Has a model design its own compact specification schema, instantiate it from a problem description, resolve ambiguities, then generate code only from the confirmed spec, for single-turn HumanEval-style coding tasks.
works.delta: The self-authored artifact is used once, immediately, by one generation pass, and reportedly helps (not hurts) stronger coding models — opposite in both structure (single-shot vs. long relay) and polarity (help vs. lock-in) to a self-designed notation that is pinned and reused/mutated across many subsequent fresh-instance turns.

works.title: Learning Agent-Compatible Context Management for Long-Horizon Tasks (AdaCoM)
works.what_it_does: Trains a separate external LLM via RL to prune/compress a frozen agent's accumulating context on web-search/deep-research tasks, finding a Fidelity-Reliability Trade-off: stronger agents benefit from high-fidelity context retention, weaker agents need more aggressive compression to stay reliable.
works.delta: The compressing party is an externally-trained RL controller acting on one continuously-growing session for a frozen agent, not a self-authored note from a fresh zero-shot instance handed to another fresh instance; no hard character/pixel budget, no certified sound-reference floor, and the crossover is about compression aggressiveness rather than self-designed vs. imposed schema.

works.title: LLM Agents Are Latent Context Managers: Eliciting Self-Managed Context via a Proprioceptive Dashboard (VISTA)
works.what_it_does: Gives agents a training-free runtime dashboard of token usage, recency, and access history over typed memory blocks so the same continuing agent can decide what to keep, archive, or drop within one long session.
works.delta: Operates within one continuous, growing agent session with recoverable archived blocks, not a hard severance between independently-sampled fresh instances where only a budgeted note/image crosses.

works.title: Plans Don't Persist: Why Context Management Is Load Bearing for LLM Agents
works.what_it_does: Uses a 'replay pairing' diagnostic (hidden-state cosine distance with/without a plan in context) to show that standard agents' internal representation of an early plan decays sharply once it leaves the context window, i.e., plans are not carried forward as persistent state.
works.delta: Evidence is gathered within a single continuing agent's hidden states on one trajectory, not across a boundary between independently-sampled fresh model instances, and offers no character/pixel budget or sound-reference certification.

works.title: Evaluating Performance Drift from Model Switching in Multi-Turn LLM Systems
works.what_it_does: Introduces a switch-matrix benchmark on CoQA/Multi-IF/IFEval that measures how much a different model/instance resuming a conversation from another's context degrades performance, relative to a no-switch baseline.
works.delta: Closest prior work in spirit (a matched no-switch baseline is structurally similar to a certified floor) but targets general instruction-following/QA degradation from model swaps, not a hidden-information deduction game, hard text/pixel budgets, notation invention, or a provably-sound truncation-based reference.

works.title: Learning to Forget: Sleep-Inspired Memory Consolidation for Resolving Proactive Interference in Large Language Models
works.what_it_does: Applies offline, sleep-inspired consolidation and algorithmic forgetting to long-term conversational/personalization memory to reduce interference between older and newer stored facts.
works.delta: Targets long-term personalization memory across many sessions of one persistent user-facing agent, not a hard-budgeted baton relayed between independently-sampled fresh instances in a single bounded game.

works.title: Text or Pixels? It Takes Half: On the Token Efficiency of Visual Text Inputs in Multimodal LLMs
works.what_it_does: Studies rendering existing textual content as an image (optical/visual-text compression) to cut input token counts for a reader model, comparing token efficiency of text vs. pixel representations of the same content.
works.delta: Compression direction is externally imposed (given text rendered to pixels for a reader), not a model's own free choice of encoding when authoring a baton; it does not test whether models spontaneously invent spatial/non-textual encodings when given a blank canvas to draw on.

threats.title: Learning Agent-Compatible Context Management for Long-Horizon Tasks (AdaCoM)
threats.overlap: Reports a capability-dependent crossover effect in how much a memory/context intervention helps: an externally-trained RL controller's optimal compression aggressiveness depends on the underlying agent's own capability, with weaker agents needing more aggressive compression and stronger agents needing high-fidelity retention — structurally similar to Blindboard's finding that memory scaffolding produces PER-MODEL crossover effects (an imposed schema lets the smallest model beat its own full-transcript score).
threats.differentiation: AdaCoM's 'memory manager' is a separately RL-trained external LLM pruning one continuously-growing session for a frozen agent — there's no severance into independently-sampled fresh instances, no hard character/pixel budget, no certified sound-reference floor, and the crossover axis is compression aggressiveness (how much to prune) rather than self-designed-vs-imposed schema (who designs the structure).
threats.claims_to_verify: Confirm (a) whether AdaCoM's crossover is genuinely about agent capability/strength rather than self- vs. externally-designed schema; (b) whether AdaCoM tests a 'self-authored schema' condition at all, which would be needed to claim any overlap with constitutional lock-in; (c) that AdaCoM uses no sound/certified reference baseline comparable to Blindboard's provably-sound truncation floor.

threats.title: Self-Spec: Model-Authored Specifications for Reliable LLM Code Generation
threats.overlap: Directly studies what happens when a model authors its own structuring artifact (a spec schema) that is then used for a downstream task, the same general question as Blindboard's 'self-designed pinned specs underperform' (constitutional lock-in) finding — but reports the opposite polarity, that self-authored specs modestly HELP stronger coding models.
threats.differentiation: Self-Spec's artifact is authored once and consumed once, in a single generation pass for one coding task — there is no repeated reuse across many subsequent turns, no chain of independently-sampled fresh instances, and no drift/mutation of the notation over generations, all of which are central to Blindboard's lock-in finding.
threats.claims_to_verify: Confirm (a) Self-Spec's spec is not reused/pinned across multiple downstream tasks or generations (i.e., it is genuinely single-shot); (b) the reported effect sizes and polarity (help, not harm) are accurate and not cherry-picked per model; (c) whether any ablation in the paper tests iterated reuse of one pinned spec, which would be the closest possible overlap to lock-in.

threats.title: LLM as a Broken Telephone: Iterative Generation Distorts Information
threats.overlap: Quantifies how information degrades across a literal chain of iterative LLM regenerations (each output feeding the next input), including accelerating distortion curves and mitigation strategies — structurally the same relay shape as Blindboard's baton-passing chain, and a natural prior-art anchor for any 'notation/information drift across generations' claim.
threats.differentiation: The chains studied are unconstrained-length natural-language regenerations (e.g., repeated translation/paraphrase) with no explicit hard character or pixel budget, no certified sound-reference floor to calibrate survivability, and no analysis of models inventing or mutating their own notation systems; it is also unclear whether each hop is a genuinely independent freshly-sampled instance versus the same model/session re-prompted repeatedly.
threats.claims_to_verify: Confirm (a) whether hops in their chains involve fresh, independently-sampled model calls with no shared state beyond the passed text (vs. same-session reprompting); (b) that no budget constraint is imposed on the passed text, making it a different regime from a hard-bottlenecked baton; (c) that they do not already report anything resembling notation invention/mutation, which would blunt the novelty of Blindboard's 'notation drift' finding.

phrases: Every fresh-instance-transmission-chain paper we found (the 'telephone game' literature) passes unbounded natural language and scores open-ended drift; none impose a hard character/pixel budget or check the transmitted artifact against a provably-sound compressed baseline the way Relay's certified deduction game does.

Every image-as-inter-agent-channel method we found (Vision Wormhole, HyLaT, latent-communication surveys) moves continuous, white-box activations between models; Relay's baton is always a genuine rendered image or plain text consumed through ordinary black-box multimodal input, so it is the only one that can even observe models defaulting to writing text inside images instead of inventing spatial notation.

Every text-as-pixels compression paper we found (Glyph, DeepSeek-OCR) has one model re-read content it rendered within its own continuous session; Relay is the only setup where the reader is a wholly separate, memoryless model instance, which is what lets it show write-render-read fidelity dissociating from downstream game performance.

No benchmark we found varies the memory scaffold itself (self-designed baton vs. imposed schema vs. full transcript) as the independent variable and reports per-model crossover effects — existing game-playing and memory-agent benchmarks treat memory scaffolding as fixed harness code, not as the manipulation under test.

The 'constitutional lock-in' and 'notation drift' related work we found studies either cooperation rule-sets in social-dilemma games or population-scale language emergence over many adapting agents; Relay is the only one of these mechanisms observed in a single lineage of frozen, non-adapting, fresh-per-turn instances inheriting one prior artifact under a certified, ground-truth-checkable task.

works.title: SVGenius: Benchmarking LLMs in SVG Understanding, Editing and Generation
works.what_it_does: Single-shot benchmark (2,377 queries, 22 models) scoring LLMs on understanding, editing, and generating SVG code across 8 task categories and 18 metrics.
works.delta: Relay never scores SVG output quality directly — it studies whether a fresh model instance can read back a self-authored, budget-constrained SVG-rendered baton well enough to keep winning a hidden-information game; there is no notion of 'good SVG' independent of game outcome.

works.title: Glyph: Scaling Context Windows via Visual-Text Compression
works.what_it_does: Renders long text into images so a VLM processes it as fewer visual tokens, achieving 3-4x context compression with accuracy comparable to native long-context text LLMs.
works.delta: Glyph compresses a single model's own existing context within one continuous session for efficiency; Relay forces independent, memoryless instances to author and re-derive meaning from a pixel-budgeted baton with zero shared context, scoring against game-correctness and a sound floor rather than token efficiency.

works.title: DeepSeek-OCR: Contexts Optical Compression
works.what_it_does: Shows text can be optically compressed into vision tokens (up to ~20x) and decoded via OCR, with ~97% precision at <10x compression degrading to ~60% at 20x.
works.delta: DeepSeek-OCR measures OCR decoding fidelity of statically rendered documents by one model/pipeline; Relay's key finding is that such read-back fidelity dissociates from downstream game performance once the reader is a separate model instance with no other shared context.

works.title: VISTA-Bench: Do Vision-Language Models Really Understand Visualized Text as Well as Pure Text?
works.what_it_does: Contrasts VLM accuracy on identical questions posed as pure text vs. rendered ('visualized') text across MMLU, MMBench, SEED-Bench, and MMMU.
works.delta: VISTA-Bench renders fixed, experimenter-authored prose under controlled conditions; Relay's images are notation a model invents for itself under compression pressure inside a live multi-turn game, not prose rendered by the researchers.

works.title: Reading, Not Thinking: Understanding and Bridging the Modality Gap When Text Becomes Pixels in Multimodal LLMs
works.what_it_does: Finds MLLMs produce 5-19x shorter, less-reasoned outputs on rendered-text documents than identical plain text, tracing the gap to suppressed reasoning effort rather than perception failure, across 7 models and 7 benchmarks.
works.delta: This diagnoses reasoning suppression when reading externally-authored document images; Relay's write-render-read dissociation is about a model's own generated image failing to preserve intended state, surfaced through downstream game correctness rather than output-length proxies.

works.title: Render-of-Thought: Rendering Textual Chain-of-Thought as Images for Visual Latent Reasoning
works.what_it_does: Renders a model's own chain-of-thought steps as images and feeds them back through the vision encoder within the same session to make latent reasoning traceable and efficient.
works.delta: Render-of-Thought is single-model, single-session self-looping of reasoning traces; Relay's pixel channel is the only bridge between otherwise fully disconnected model instances across a multi-turn game — nothing but the rendered baton survives between 'generations.'

works.title: Optical Reasoning: Rethinking Images as an Expressive Reasoning Medium Beyond Text
works.what_it_does: Has a single model perform typographic/graphical 'optical' chain-of-thought in images instead of text, cutting reasoning tokens ~16-29% at matched or better accuracy.
works.delta: Optical Reasoning optimizes one model's own visual scratchpad within a session for token efficiency; Relay imposes a hard budget as a cross-instance survivability test and certifies it against a provably-sound non-LLM baseline, which has no analogue here.

works.title: When LLMs Play the Telephone Game: Cumulative Changes and Attractors in Iterated Cultural Transmissions
works.what_it_does: Passes full text through a chain of LLM instances (translation, paraphrase, summarization) and tracks how properties like toxicity, positivity, and length drift toward 'attractor' states over many iterations.
works.delta: Closest mechanic match (a chain where each link only sees the prior link's output), but passes unbounded text with no fixed budget, no ground-truth-checkable task, and no sound reference baseline — Relay adds an explicit character/pixel budget, a certified-solvable deduction game, and a provably-sound compressed baseline that certifies which budgets are survivable.

works.title: LLM as a Broken Telephone: Iterative Generation Distorts Information
works.what_it_does: Runs iterative back-translation/generation chains and measures factuality and relevance decay over up to 50 iterations, using translation as the transmission task.
works.delta: Same family as the ICLR 2025 telephone-game paper — studies open-ended distortion of narrative/translation content with no size budget, no image channel, and no verifiable game outcome to score against a sound floor.

works.title: The Vision Wormhole: Latent-Space Communication in Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Systems
works.what_it_does: Maps heterogeneous agents' continuous reasoning traces into a shared latent space via a Universal Visual Codec and injects them directly into a receiver's vision-encoder pathway, treating the visual interface as a text-free communication port.
works.delta: Vision Wormhole transmits continuous activations requiring instrumented, white-box access to both models' internals and never actually renders an image; Relay's baton is a genuine rendered image consumed as ordinary pixel input by a frozen, black-box instance, which is what lets it observe models defaulting to writing text inside images rather than inventing spatial encoding.

works.title: HyLaT: Efficient Multi-Agent Communication via Hybrid Latent-Text Protocol
works.what_it_does: Trains agents via a two-stage framework to mix an efficient-but-opaque latent channel with concise natural-language snippets for interpretable multi-round agent communication.
